# P34.31 — Living-record test lint (G6) + nightly advance backtest

**Requirement ids:** **SIG-ENG-040** (satisfied — G6 `living-record-tests`:
the lint gates `make check`; the nightly replays tests across legitimate
record advances) · **SIG-MEM-004** (cited — verdicts stay re-judgeable; the
matrix's own uniqueness check is a registered invariant) · **SIG-MEM-006**
(cited — append-only registers per change; owner P34.7) · **Base:**
`r11/P34.30-memory-cutover-disposition-and-transition-rule` (stacked; merge
after P34.30) · **Ticket:**
`docs/tickets/236_P34.31__living-record-test-lint.md` (manifest row 236 —
Round 11 / P34, sub-round 11A; depends SEED-03) · **Gate:** no pause ·
**Live stage:** none (`live_verification=false`) · **Production
mutations:** none · **CI config changed: yes** — `nightly.yml` gains the
`backtest` stage (read-only `git archive` replay; feeds the report gate and
artifact upload; no secrets, no new jobs), and `ci.yml`'s `python` job gains
`fetch-depth: 0` (the backtest's real-tree floor test replays first-parent
history; a depth-1 checkout makes its transitions vacuous — same checkout
the docs job and the nightly replay stage already use).

## Why

Build memory is living state — the LEDGER cursor, BUILD_INDEX, DEFERRALS,
the coverage matrix, readouts, the projection, the build README's row
range, the manifest — so a test asserting a record's *current* value fails
not because code broke but because the record did its job. That is the
#165/#179/#185 shape (an `EXPECTED_ROWS` constant, a pinned cursor value),
and BM-TEST-01 bans it. SEED-03 converted the mapped pins and the §8b
`living-pin?` grep warned — but the grep matched text unscoped: three
`tmp_path` fixture constants (named `KEYS`) tripped it while a real pin
phrased differently would sail through. This row replaces the heuristic
with a declared policy + an AST lint in `make check`, and adds the nightly
replay that catches a pin at exactly the transition that legitimately
changes the value.

## What this ships

- **`living-record-policy/1`** —
  `docs/build/tools/record_policy/living_records.toml`: the living paths
  and globs (LEDGER, BUILD_INDEX, DEFERRALS, the coverage matrix, backlog
  register, readouts, `reports/current/`, `reports/obligations/`,
  `reports/spend/`, the build README, the manifest, the ADR index, root
  README/CHANGELOG), the frozen artifacts (living wins on overlap), the
  LEDGER current-state keys, the status vocabulary, the named-id shapes,
  and the `[invariants.allowed]` escape-hatch registry with a reason per
  key. One declaration feeds the lint, the backtest and the §8b check.
- **`docs/build/tools/living_record_lint.py` + the `make check` driver.**
  A test is *evaluated* only when it reads a living path anchored at the
  repository root — `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]` / `REPO_ROOT`
  expressions, `read_text()`/`open()`/`exists()`/`glob()`, repo-relative
  literals bound to a helper's path parameter (transitively), constant
  loop iterables, and `git show <sha>:<path>` snapshots (recorded,
  sanctioned). `tmp_path` fixtures and validator calls
  (`audit_current_state.audit(REPO_ROOT)`) are never evaluated. An
  evaluated test fails on: a current-state `key: value` literal; an
  assertion pairing a status word with a record id or asserting a status
  of a living-derived value (including `derived == "P33.8"` id equality);
  `len(<living-derived>) == <int>`; a literal row-range/calendar date
  inside an assertion. Docstrings and f-string segments are not literals.
  `tests/unit/test_no_living_record_pins.py` drives it under `make check`
  — violations, unregistered marks, and a vacuous run all fail.
- **The registered escape hatch** —
  `@pytest.mark.living_record_invariant("<key>")`, each key landing its
  own commit: `coverage-row-uniqueness`,
  `build-index-append-only-history`, `backlog-terminal-history` (the three
  SEED-03-registered), `gate-readout-state-vocabulary` (the conditional
  PENDING/SIGNED provenance check) and `ledger-cursor-done-consistency`
  ("never DONE while a row is next" — a relation, not a pin). Every key
  is exercised by a rule the lint actually fires.
- **`test_repo_docs_current_state.py` conversion** — the canonical host is
  derived from `web/astro.config`'s `site:` field (reference resolution)
  instead of pinning `surveillancegraph.org` inside living files.
- **§8b supersession** — `check-build-memory.sh` drops the `living-pin?`
  grep (its three warnings were the fixture false positives) and now
  structurally requires the policy/lint/driver wiring and runs the lint
  when a tomllib-capable python3 is present — violations, not warnings.
- **`docs/build/tools/living_record_backtest.py` +
  `living-backtest/1`** — the nightly advance backtest: for every
  first-parent transition C → C′ in the window where C′ changed a living
  record, it archives C′ into a temp tree (read-only — no worktree, no
  checkout), overlays C's evaluated test files, runs exactly those tests
  under the caller's interpreter, and classifies each failure:
  `pin-broken` (identical test red on C′ — a living-record pin caught at
  the transition that broke it), `converted-in-head`, `removed-in-head`,
  `infra`. C′-only test files stay in place — the coverage checker cites
  tests as evidence. `nightly.yml` gains the `continue-on-error` stage
  feeding the report gate + artifact upload; `fetch-depth: 0` supplies the
  full first-parent history; a vacuous run exits 3.
- **Docs + decisions** — `tests/AGENTS.md` records the convention (living
  records read through validators or snapshot commits; a failing pin is
  converted or deleted, never relaxed — OM-15); ADR-197 records the owned
  design (declared policy over heuristics, the real-tree/fixture/channel
  distinction, the registry escape hatch, the backtest shape + its
  documented fidelity caveat); `D-P34.31-1` (kind V) defers observing the
  first scheduled backtest run, anchored `D-P34.31-1:e0`.

## Deviations

- **OM-16 size budget flagged:** ≈ 2,150 changed lines excluding generated
  (spec, ADR index, `BACKLOG.md` mirror, `current/*`, `events.jsonl`) and
  build-memory bookkeeping vs the S budget ≤ 1,500 — the AST lint (871) +
  its suite (308) + the backtest (300) + its suite (199) + policy (150) +
  ADR (125) + wiring/tests/docs ≈ 200. The lint, backtest and policy are one
  atomic G6 contract; no split is possible mid-run, so the overage is
  disclosed rather than hidden (same disposition as P34.3).
- One commit body (7cb47ba8) lost the word `` `migrate` `` to shell backtick
  evaluation — cosmetic; committed forward per the commit-forward-only rule.
- Three head CI reds fixed forward on this PR, recorded not smoothed: two
  stale projection digests on record edits (regen commits, same class as
  P34.28/P34.30 closeouts) and the backtest floor test going vacuous under
  the python job's depth-1 checkout (`fetch-depth: 0` + a fails-if-removed
  workflow pin). The full-history replay then surfaced two real semantics
  bugs, fixed in-branch: (1) `pin-broken`/`converted-in-head`/
  `removed-in-head` compared the failing test's source at C against
  **C′**, but the classes mean repo **HEAD** — a pin converted after C′
  mislabeled as a live finding (permanent noise on real history); and (2)
  on the merge ref's main-side history the floor replayed the P34.23
  closeout head `7e54296c`, whose own committed `check_coverage_matrix`
  flags its own tree (SIG-REL-014 still routed to the ticket it lands —
  the documented fix-forward closeout convention). The failing test is a
  lint-clean validator, not a pin: pin-family classification is now keyed
  to the lint's own definition (a failure counts as
  `pin-broken`/`converted-in-head`/`removed-in-head` only when the C-era
  test violates the policy unexempted); lint-clean or registered-exempt
  failures classify **`broken-tree`** — the transition head's own tree
  trips a legitimate invariant — reported per transition with the
  replayed run's output tail, never a gate failure. The replay now also
  covers the most *recent* transitions under `--max-transitions`, as
  documented. ADR-197 §5 amended (unmerged, in-branch; trigger section
  untouched).
